subject: MedTrust hosting constraints and network isolation recap
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@medtrust.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@medtrust.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: MedTrust hosting constraints and network isolation recap

Hi Nora / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Short summary below so we all have the same picture and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of customer goals and drivers:
- Primary goal: run PHI-sensitive inference for clinical summarization and claims triage inside an isolated environment (no PHI egress).
- Driver: regulatory and payer contracts require strict residency and audit controls plus hardware isolation for one-year pilot.
- Success metric: <50ms median token latency for typical throughput of ~10 concurrent user sessions; retention of audit logs for 7 years.

Key constraints you called out:
- Must run in MedTrust's dedicated VPC (no shared tenancy).
- No outbound internet egress from inference hosts except via a controlled proxy; all third-party calls must traverse MedTrust-managed proxy.
- Air-gap/segmented mode desired for environments processing highest-sensitivity data (permissioned on a per-project basis).
- KMS integration: customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) for model artifacts and KV cache encryption.
- Ports: only HTTPS (443) outbound allowed from the inference subnet; inbound only from internal app tier via VPC peering. No public IPs.

Technical notes / potential blockers:
- We confirmed Redwood Private can be deployed into a customer VPC using our private control plane, but the standard host-agent needs an outbound connection for telemetry and control plane operations. We discussed a proxy+whitelist approach; Samir said MedTrust security will not allow direct control-plane outbound to our hosted endpoints.
- Air-gapped option: we can package an on-prem appliance and run with an offline control plane; this requires a short engineering SOW and additional compliance attestations (SOC2 artifacts).
- Audit logs: retention to 7 years will need an archive pipeline (S3 Glacier or equivalent) — MedTrust will own archival storage but Redwood needs object encryption with CMK and a weekly export job.

Immediate next steps (mutual action items):
1) Aditya to send the network checklist + minimal port/endpoint list for a connectivity test (attached).
2) MedTrust (Samir) to confirm proxy hostname(s) and the allowed egress FQDNs by next Tue 03/30.
3) Ben to scope a short SOW covering the offline control-plane build and compliance package; initial estimate due 04/04.
4) Schedule a 1-hour connectivity test window (suggested: Thu 03/31, 16:00–17:00 ET).

Attachments: medtrust_network_checklist.csv (network ports, IP ranges, FQDNs) — uploaded to the shared Drive as well: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/medtrust-network-checklist

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the checklist and a short note on the offline SOW scope.

—
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@medtrust.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.k@medtrust.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MedTrust hosting constraints and network isolation recap

Aditya —

Appreciate the notes and the clarity. A couple of clarifications from our side after syncing with infra/security: 
- We cannot permit any persistent outbound connections to vendor-hosted control planes. Short-lived certificate-based connections initiated from our side may be acceptable, but we need the option to fully disable outbound egress in the highest-sensitivity environment.
- The proxy will be an explicit requirement. We will provide the proxy FQDNs and an internal NAT IP range; only those will be allowed.
- For audit retention, we already have an S3 archival strategy; we will need Redwood to support a weekly push of anonymized audit bundles to our archival bucket with CMK encryption.

We are aligned on the proposed test window Thu 03/31 16:00 ET — Samir will validate with the networking team and confirm by EOD tomorrow.

One ask: please include a short 'offline control plane' risk checklist in the SOW so our Risk team can review it quickly.

Thanks,
Nora
Director, Infrastructure Security
MedTrust Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@medtrust.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@medtrust.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MedTrust hosting constraints and network isolation recap

Nora / Samir —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and flags. A few commitments from Redwood side: 
- I’ll own the SOW for the offline control plane and include the risk checklist Aditya referenced. Expect a draft by COB 04/04 that will explicitly call out: build steps, verification gating, telemetry opt-out, and the SOC2 artifact list.
- We can support customer-managed CMK usage for model artifacts and KV cache; we will add explicit instructions for key rotation and access logging in the SOW.
- For the connectivity test, Aditya will share the exact IPs/FQDNs we will attempt to reach; our test is limited to TLS handshake and an agent registration attempt — no model payloads will be sent.

Attaching the initial network checklist we use for VPC deployments (medtrust_network_checklist.csv) and a redacted SOC2 evidence request list to speed up your Risk review (SOC2_evidence_request.pdf).

Proposed small next-step: 30-min technical sync with your networking lead after the connectivity test to unblock the SOW.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (646) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: medtrust_network_checklist.csv (CSV), SOC2_evidence_request.pdf (PDF)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@medtrust.com>, Nora Patel <nora.patel@medtrust.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: MedTrust hosting constraints and network isolation recap

Samir / Nora — forwarding a quick note so you have a single contact for SOW and contract questions. 

We will treat the offline control plane SOW as a separate line item to the hosting agreement; Ben will own the technical SOW, I’ll own commercial terms and any compliance addendum.

Quick asks from Redwood legal/compliance for Risk review: 
- Short summary of expected data types/processes (we have that from the call — clinical summaries + claims metadata).
- Confirmation on retention timeline (7 years) and archival target bucket ARN.
- Point of contact for key rotation and HSM/KMS ownership.

If we can get those three items this week, I’ll push an early commercial outline and a draft addendum for your legal team to  review.

Thanks — looking forward to the connectivity test confirmation.

—
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0177
